title: Seven retry-safe turn handlers are copy-pasted and have drifted
note: Duplication confirmed: server/appwire_runtime.go:1592-1830 handlers repeat trim/lockRetrySafeMutation/RLock-copy/Unavailable/refreshFacets/NormalizeClientMutationError; ClientMutationID TrimSpace appears 10x non-test. The 'input required' (1774) vs 'input is required' (1622,1668) drift is copy only. The claimed DrainAsSteer 'missing HasContent check' is likely intentional: TurnDrainAsSteerParams.Input is documented as optional ('lets clients atomically append the current composer payload before the drain', types.go ~2719) and drain's job is to pop queued entries, so requiring input would be a behavior break. ThreadID drift is real (Queue/Drain/Promote pass '' because the params types have no ThreadID, types.go:2636,2719). Severity medium: real PR, but the 'drift already live' part is mostly cosmetic.
revised_fix_plan: 1) Characterization tests per handler on error codes/EvenerErrorInfo. 2) Extract one retrySafeMutation helper (trim, lock, nil-check, call, refreshFacets(facetQueue), error normalization). 3) Extract one input-gate helper for Start/Steer/Queue/Drain parameterized by 'content required' (true for Start/Steer/Queue, false for Drain) rather than 'fixing' Drain; unify the one message string. 4) The embedded MutationIdentity struct is optional and needs Jesse plus generator support; skip unless wanted.

title: RecordAppEvent and RecordDescendantAppEvent duplicate the projection switch; both are 140-180 line functions
note: Overstated. Opened both switches (appwire_runtime.go:430-490 and 727-780). Only the TaskUpdatedParams case is truly identical (~14 lines: accept, routeOwner blanking, taskCarrierTargetsLocked loop, applyTaskCarrierLocked, pending append). ThreadStarted differs materially (root vs descendant seeding, parentRef, Access, shared-task fallback). Goal/Notes/Urls bodies are 1-4 lines each, and the root side also bumps goal/notes/urlsCarrierGeneration fences that descendants deliberately lack, so a shared sink would need fence hooks and the claimed -120 LOC is too high. The sourceID defaulting duplication is minor.
revised_fix_plan: Extract only the TaskUpdated routing block into one helper (e.g. routeTaskUpdateLocked(item, threadID, params) []pendingAppNotification) used by both callers; leave goal/notes/urls inline. About -20 LOC. Guard with existing descendant_watches and notes tests.

title: Callback-field boilerplate: 25 Set*Func setters, 39 RLock-copy-nil blocks, a 50-method single-impl interface
note: Mechanics confirmed but counts drift: 27 Set*Func setters (server.go 20, session_activity 4, runtime 3), 51 s.mu.RLock() and 21 appwire.Unavailable( in appwire_runtime.go. Four session-activity handlers (appwire_session_activity.go:26-110) are indeed identical but for field and type. serveServer (cmd/evener/serve.go:101) is single-impl in production but is a deliberate test seam: 10+ test files inject fakes through deps.newServer (e.g. sessionControlIdentityServer in serve_state_test.go:280, newResidualServeServer in serve_residual_fuzz_test.go:314), so deleting it is a large test migration, not a cleanup. JobsListResponse.Data is any (types.go:2900), real.
revised_fix_plan: Do the safe parts: one generic sessionActivityHandler[P,R] (-50), give JobsListResponse.Data a real type and regenerate, and pin one unwired-hook policy. Treat the generic hook[T] and serveServer shrinking as separate, Jesse-approved proposals (serveServer is a test seam). Do not delete serveServer in this change.

title: Thread envelope keeps two authorities (sampled facets and typed carriers) plus five generation fences
note: Comments at thread_envelope.go:27,291-292 and appwire_runtime.go:864 do say 'old-producer compatibility', and the five carrier counters exist (thread_envelope.go:67-84, 361-365). But the 'producers are in the same binary' premise is incomplete: TaskPublicationEpoch/Revision are json:"-" (agent/events/payloads.go:47-50), so any event that is deserialized or replayed (checkpoint recovery, resume) carries zero metadata and legitimately takes the legacy path. The sampled path is the recovery path after restart, which AGENTS.md says to preserve. Removing it is not shown to be safe; fix plan itself says to audit first. Downgraded to low until the audit shows zero-metadata events cannot occur.
revised_fix_plan: Only after an audit of replay/resume paths proves no zero-metadata task events reach the projector: then consider collapsing the five counters into one per-identity generation. Otherwise leave behavior and only rename 'legacy/old-producer' comments to say what zero metadata means (replayed or ownerless events).

title: types.go is a 5,898-line monolith; method constants and retry-safe method tables are scattered and disagree
note: 5,898 lines and 365 types confirmed (comment lines are actually ~2,280 by a broader count, not 1,190). Method constants outside types.go confirmed (keybindings.go:13, agents_doc.go:9, transcript_display.go:12). ValidateMutationParams (protocol.go:323) rebuilds its map per call and includes MethodUrlsRemove, while retrySafeMutationMethods (errors.go:923) and TS RETRY_SAFE_MUTATION_METHODS (dispatcher.ts:313) both list the same 9 without urls/remove. That is the Go/TS pair pinned equal by a test; urls/remove omission may be deliberate (not backpressure-refusable) so 'disagree' is a question for Jesse, not proven drift. File split is subjective navigability.
revised_fix_plan: 1) Hoist the ValidateMutationParams map to a package var (tiny, safe). 2) Ask Jesse whether urls/remove should be retry-safe; if not, document why it differs. 3) Mechanical types.go split only with byte-identical go generate output as proof, as an opportunistic PR.

title: Four near-identical stamp*OnStatusChange functions wrapped in ~150 lines of comments
note: Four functions confirmed at appwire_runtime.go:557,1036,1089,1147 called back to back (543-545). But they are not purely identical: stampFailureCountOnStatusChange has a side effect (writes s.appPushedFailedToolCalls under s.mu.Lock) and an 'unmeasured' skip, stampAskPendingOnStatusChange always stamps, so folding them under one RLock needs care with the pushed-count write ordering. revised_fix_plan: Extract only the shared type-assertion prelude (e.g. asRootStatusChange(method, params)) and keep the per-field logic; skip the single-RLock consolidation unless a test shows it matters. About -20 LOC.
